This induces a stochastic process where errors are categorized into known wrong responses versus correct ones. The 'error_frequency_analysis' primitive captures the empirical distribution of these outcomes, enabling probabilistic inference about learning efficacy. The 'cognitive_rehearsal_model' extends this by introducing temporal dynamics, where repeated exposure modifies memory strength. These primitives form a dual structure: one rooted in Bayesian updating of error probabilities (GSI), the other in Markovian transitions of cognitive states (GSE). Failure modes occur when practice duration becomes insufficient or when feedback delays exceed cognitive thresholds, leading to divergence from intended learning paths.
